_comment: Fragment 23 — D-66, G62b decided: ESLint CLI with next/core-web-vitals. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-66 — G62b: Migrate to the ESLint CLI
nodes.description: Lint moves from next lint to the ESLint CLI with a flat config extending next/core-web-vitals. The package.json lint script repoints from next lint to eslint dot. Everything needed is already installed — eslint 9.39.5, eslint-config-next 15.5.23, @eslint/eslintrc 3.3.6 — so no dependency is added. The config file itself is Stage A and was not created.
nodes.rationale: Closes G62b as a decision, not a fix. G62a remains open — typecheck still exits 2 with ten errors, so R3 DoD D-4 is still unachievable. Does not settle Q6, though a working ESLint CLI in CI makes eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds far less load-bearing.

nodes.label: Dropping Lint Was Never Actually an Option
nodes.description: G62b was framed as migrate, or drop lint from CI and record why. AC-NF-03 requires that typecheck, lint and tests all execute and must pass, so dropping lint would contradict a recorded acceptance criterion — a Modular_PRD tier-two amendment rather than a CI config choice.
nodes.rationale: The governing set had already answered the question; the second option was illusory. Recorded so a later reader does not reopen it as though it were open. AC-NF-03 is left unchanged — the decision keeps lint in CI rather than amending the criterion away.

nodes.label: Measurement Dissolved the Preset Question
nodes.description: The real fork was Base versus Strict. Measured with throwaway configs outside the repository: next and next/core-web-vitals each linted 21 files with zero errors and zero warnings. Identical, so the stricter preset costs nothing today and is chosen.
nodes.rationale: A question measurement answered for free — it was about to be put to the Chief Editor as a trade-off, and there is no trade-off today. Recorded as a counterweight to the project's dominant failure mode: four times a claim was derived from a summary instead of the thing. Here the thing was checked first and the question disappeared.

nodes.label: G62a Is a Code Fix; G62b Is a Config Addition
nodes.description: G62a is real remediation — ten implicit-any errors across two lib/supabase files. G62b has zero findings to fix; lint already passes and has simply never been able to run for want of a config. The two were bundled as one gap and are not one task.
nodes.rationale: Recorded because bundling them would have made Stage A look like uniform remediation work when half of it is a single file with no findings behind it.
